problem_text:
A city planner needs to distribute a fixed water supply across 19 different districts to maximize the total expected water quality improvement.  
The characteristics of each district are as follows:  
* District A: expected improvement is 0.122, contamination level is 0.229, allocation bounds [0.065, 0.487]  
* District B: expected improvement is 0.133, contamination level is 0.188, allocation bounds [0.033, 0.893]  
* District C: expected improvement is 0.118, contamination level is 0.098, allocation bounds [0.010, 0.304]  
* District D: expected improvement is 0.088, contamination level is 0.080, allocation bounds [0.029, 0.591]  
* District E: expected improvement is 0.178, contamination level is 0.159, allocation bounds [0.048, 0.713]  
* District F: expected improvement is 0.099, contamination level is 0.047, allocation bounds [0.033, 0.369]  
* District G: expected improvement is 0.045, contamination level is 0.168, allocation bounds [0.006, 0.300]  
* District H: expected improvement is 0.100, contamination level is 0.174, allocation bounds [0.074, 0.662]  
* District I: expected improvement is 0.076, contamination level is 0.095, allocation bounds [0.067, 0.373]  
* District J: expected improvement is 0.188, contamination level is 0.229, allocation bounds [0.074, 0.358]  
* District K: expected improvement is 0.148, contamination level is 0.124, allocation bounds [0.005, 0.423]  
* District L: expected improvement is 0.104, contamination level is 0.127, allocation bounds [0.021, 0.584]  
* District M: expected improvement is 0.097, contamination level is 0.012, allocation bounds [0.014, 0.800]  
* District N: expected improvement is 0.096, contamination level is 0.244, allocation bounds [0.074, 0.566]  
* District O: expected improvement is 0.094, contamination level is 0.264, allocation bounds [0.050, 0.333]  
* District P: expected improvement is 0.025, contamination level is 0.143, allocation bounds [0.022, 0.373]  
* District Q: expected improvement is 0.121, contamination level is 0.026, allocation bounds [0.068, 0.543]  
* District R: expected improvement is 0.192, contamination level is 0.026, allocation bounds [0.085, 0.890]  
* District S: expected improvement is 0.096, contamination level is 0.251, allocation bounds [0.030, 0.792]  

Each district must receive a proportion of the total water supply within its specified allocation bounds, and the sum of all proportions must equal one. To ensure equitable access, the group of priority districts, represented by the subset L = {A, C, D, G, M, N, O, P, S}, must collectively receive at least 0.313 of the total water supply.  
Additionally, the overall system contamination index must not exceed 0.175, and the total expected improvement in water quality must be at least 0.078.  
Determine the optimal water allocation weights that maximize total expected improvement while satisfying all constraints.
